newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Bank unlikely to securitise mortgages at moment.
newsitem.headline: HK Bank unlikely to securitise mortgages at moment.

text.p: Hong Kong's planned mortgage corporation was a good idea in the long term, but Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp was unlikely to securitise its mortgages under current circumstances, its general manager said on Friday.
"In principle, our bank has no objection whatsoever to securitising retail mortgages and selling them down to a mortgage corporation," Christopher Langley told reporters.
But whether the bank would do so depended on the market situation, the shape of its balance sheet, its preferred use of funds and similar factors at the time, he said.
"Given the current situation there would be very, very little likelihood, frankly, of actually selling down any retail mortgages at the moment," he said.
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the territory's de facto central bank, has cited the establishment of Hong Kong Mortgage Corp Ltd as a major task for the next year.

Langley said the Hong Kong Association of Banks (HKAB), and Hongkong Bank through HKAB, had studied the HKMA's draft memorandum on the proposed mortgage corporation and saw no particular points of contention or concern.

"The mortgage corporation in the longer term will encourage the development of a mortgage-backed securities industry here, which is a good thing in terms of broadening and deepening the local domestic bond market," he said.
Hongkong Bank itself had studied the issue a few years ago and determined securitisation was entirely feasible, he said.

But Langley said banks tended to like carrying mortgages, which were high quality assets, on their balance sheets, although individual banks may have money management requirements that led them to securitise mortgages and raise cash.
Choosing whether or not to securitise was not a decision to be made a long time in advance, he added.
Hongkong Bank is a unit of HSBC Holdings Plc .
